description: A Product Director must approve the production launch policy for a self-serve API-key rotation workflow, including the client grace period, customer notice, audit retention, and follow-up commitments, with input from backend engineering, customer success, and security.

shared_context.S1: The self-serve API-key rotation workflow has passed its planned staging tests and is scheduled for production launch next Monday.
shared_context.S2: Maya has final approval authority for the launch policy.
shared_context.S3: The current draft policy enables the workflow for all eligible customers, gives clients a 24-hour transition period, provides no advance customer notice, and retains ordinary rotation logs for 30 days.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal go-live review, backend engineering, customer success, and security each report any operational or customer-facing requirements before Maya approves the policy.

PF1.text: While testing an unrelated SDK issue this morning, Ethan confirmed that the legacy client can submit the rotation request twice and needs an exactly 48-hour idempotency grace period to avoid invalidating both keys; he has not updated the launch ticket because the confirmation came after the test review.

PF2.text: Leila confirmed with the account team today that the Northstar enterprise agreement requires exactly 14 calendar days' advance notice before any API-key policy change affecting its integrations; she has not added the clause to the launch document because legal confirmed it only an hour ago.

PF3.text: During a separate audit review this afternoon, Ravi confirmed that privileged key-rotation events must be stored in immutable audit storage for exactly 365 days; the current 30-day log setting would not satisfy that control, and he has not opened the security finding yet.

acceptance_conditions: The workflow must launch next Monday.
The client idempotency grace period must be exactly 48 hours.
Northstar must receive exactly 14 calendar days of advance notice.
Privileged key-rotation events must use immutable audit storage.
Privileged key-rotation events must be retained for exactly 365 days.
A legacy-client compatibility commitment must be recorded.
A Northstar customer-notice commitment must be recorded.
A security-audit retention commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The draft gives clients 24 hours, while PF1 changes the required client idempotency grace period to exactly 48 hours and adds the legacy-client compatibility commitment.
The draft provides no advance notice, while PF2 changes Northstar's required notice to exactly 14 calendar days and adds the Northstar customer-notice commitment.
The draft retains ordinary logs for 30 days, while PF3 changes privileged-event handling to immutable storage with exactly 365 days of retention and adds the security-audit retention commitment.
